limitations: No solver unit test establishes performance on all benchmark tasks; parent conducts serialized GPU evaluation
CHOMP and TrajOpt main comparison must retain adaptation labels
No finite collision samples establish mathematical continuous collision safety
Native local objective of CHOMP/STOMP/TrajOpt is composite/squared smoothness, not exact benchmark path length
Common validator applies derivative control hull bounds; it is a conservative numerical admissibility rule

review_history.scope: Earlier source review; original tests and changes are retained under their existing top-level keys.

latest_review_scope: Read-only source/archived-audit check; no new planner, model, solver or GPU execution.
scsto_identity: SCSTO is EI_ZO/minimum_time, not a separate stable method ID.
source_compatibility: Reviewed method sources are byte-identical to 88f50536d59e6e617afcaece9bc01d214005746f at statistics commit 59bbfc922f4cc053a0a0ef89aa714b176875a0b1; the latter changes only result aggregation and its tests.
shared_notes: STOMP uses an unmodified official core, while canonical cost/noise callbacks are adaptations; label does not mean the whole author task setup was copied.

CHOMP is explicitly a C-space-functional adaptation with covariant descent. TrajOpt is author SQP/BPMPD core with sampled collision adaptation. Their native smoothness/collision or squared-difference objectives are not the evaluated PWL length.

Whole-flow and fixed_initial_regions results must remain distinct. Fixed-mode eligibility uses the sealed original front-end stage, regardless of original solver success; both backends newly receive the same 60 s budget. Later graph expansion/repair is retained.

All scores require the common numerical validator. Finite collision sampling does not prove continuous collision freedom; derivative control-hull bounds are conservative continuous-segment motion-limit checks.

Normal nonconvergence and hard-query failure remain valid method observations. Native backend exceptions remain infrastructure_error. Saved valid nonconverged candidates can count only under the strict common evidence rule, never when process/timeout/array evidence contradicts them.
Keep first terminal attempt for scores; an unscored diagnostic or later witness never replaces it. No assertion of completed legacy NTO coverage is made here.

known_backend_issue.status: Unfixed upstream backend issue; scored observations unchanged. No broad NTO exclusion follows from it.

actual_coverage_status: All declared current smoke/dev/test combinations and the explicit shared-initial-region cohort are complete. Smoke is coverage evidence only; performance comparisons use the named selected cohorts. Counts are cross-checked from final records.csv and summary.csv without replanning or recollection.
historical_evidence_scope: Original tests, changes and limitations are retained as earlier audit evidence; current resolved config disables the diagnostic OMPL progress observer. Historical observer settings in changes are not active main-baseline settings.

actual_coverage_evidence.counts_denominator: Success counts divide by legal finished queries, not registered invalid-input slots; paired seed repetitions are query observations, not independent scenes.
actual_coverage_evidence.smoke_scope: First terminal coverage from results/smoke and results/nto_legacy_smoke only; not an added selected comparison.
